=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:lines 1978-1980, `if cached_runs_snapshot and all("event" in item for item in cached_runs_snapshot):` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new `all("event" in item for item in cached_runs_snapshot)` predicate is an O(n) scan over every cached item, executed on every 304 response.
  WHY: For large snapshots (thousands of items) the per-tick scan adds non-trivial wall-clock work to a path designed to be a cheap cache hit. The cost is bounded by the snapshot size, so it cannot deadlock or OOM, but it shifts work back onto the 304 path that was meant to avoid it.
- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:lines 1978-1980, `if cached_runs_snapshot and all("event" in item for item in cached_runs_snapshot):` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cache-snapshot validity check uses an ad-hoc field-presence predicate (`all("event" in item for item in cached_runs_snapshot)`) rather than a single schema-version gate, so any future field the origin classifier relies on will require another implicit `in` check here.
  WHY: A future change that adds another stamp field to `_stamp_run_origin` (for example, `pull_request_base_repository` if the trust rule is tightened) would silently classify every cached row as `origin_unknown` until the cache is rebuilt, repeating the same legacy-snapshot failure mode this PR fixed. There is no single source of truth that flags a stale snapshot shape.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
